findings.statement: The lib/auth-helpers.ts 'wrapper' is a leaky facade: it re-exports vendor functions and returns Amplify's AuthSession/AuthUser unchanged.
findings.note: Looks like a boundary and earns no credit as one — the vendor's shape passes straight through to every caller.

evidence.quote: import { fetchAuthSession, getCurrentUser, signOut, AuthSession, AuthUser } from 'aws-amplify/auth';

findings.statement: Amplify's AuthSession type crosses into app-layer component state and an exported function return type in UserBadge.tsx.
Auth is imported directly from aws-amplify/auth and used inline at each call site — the API client and components — with no injected port.
The only auth test mocks aws-amplify/auth and asserts on the vendor's AuthSession shape — it passes today and dies on migration.
No conformance/contract suite exists that tests the auth boundary independently of the vendor.
checked_patterns: conformance/contract suite against the boundary (e.g. runAuthContractTests / an AuthPort shape every adapter must pass)
tests asserting on a domain Principal / AuthError shape rather than the vendor's AuthSession
adapter-conformance tests exercising an injected port

findings.statement: There is no SSR/server auth surface, so no client/server split exists to absorb — the concern does not arise.
checked_patterns: typeof window / execution-context branching to obtain auth

findings.statement: Token storage is left at the Amplify v6 default (browser localStorage) — no custom storage adapter or custom tokenProvider is configured.
findings.note: Amplify v6 detected. Amplify.configure passes only the Cognito user-pool block; no storage customization anywhere.
checked_patterns: custom tokenProvider passed to Amplify.configure(config, { Auth: { tokenProvider } }) [v6 deep customization]
built-in selectors defaultStorage / sessionStorage / new CookieStorage() passed to setKeyValueStorage [v6 look-alike, not a custom adapter]
cookieStorage: { domain, path, expires, ... } inside Amplify.configure({ Auth }) [v5 built-in cookie selector]
storage: <class> inside Amplify.configure({ Auth }) [v5 custom storage class]

findings.statement: Refresh is inherited vendor magic: a bare fetchAuthSession() in the axios request interceptor, with no single-flight dedup and no onSessionExpired failure path.
findings.note: Amplify's silent refresh works only because tokens are JS-readable; it breaks the day storage moves to HttpOnly cookies.

findings.statement: Cognito-namespaced claims (cognito:groups) are read inline for authorization decisions, with hard-coded role strings, in two separate components.
findings.note: Serves both the identity-provider axis (Cognito-specific claim surface in app code) and the authorization axis (inline claim/role reads, no policy layer).

findings.statement: Page-level code calls fetchUserAttributes directly, types state as the vendor's FetchUserAttributesOutput, and reads a custom: attribute inline.
The ID token (not the access token) is attached as the outbound API Authorization header — authentication coupled to authorization.

b1_anti_corruption.note: Vendor AuthSession / AuthUser / FetchUserAttributesOutput cross into component state, page state, and exported return types; the auth-helpers.ts wrapper returns AuthSession unchanged.

b2_injected.note: Auth is imported directly from aws-amplify/auth at each call site (API client, components); there is no injected AuthPort.

b3_contract_tested.note: No contract suite; the only auth test mocks the vendor and asserts on its shape.

b4_client_server_split.note: Client-only React SPA; no SSR/server auth surface exists, so the client/server split does not arise.

cognito.note: Amplify v6; no setKeyValueStorage or custom tokenProvider — default browser localStorage.

storage.recommended_seam: Plug a custom class implementing KeyValueStorageInterface into cognitoUserPoolsTokenProvider.setKeyValueStorage, behind an auth boundary, so where tokens live becomes one adapter's decision rather than the localStorage default. (Note: this overrides the TokenStore only; identityId stays in localStorage if Identity Pools are used.)

cost_evidence.basis: Storage is unconfigured (default localStorage) and there is no boundary or storage seam to plug an adapter into, so the retrofit is introducing the seam plus config — contained, but the JS-readable-token dependency ties it to the refresh path.

cognito.note: Bare fetchAuthSession() in the axios interceptor; no single-flight, no onSessionExpired.

refresh.recommended_seam: Own refresh at the API-client seam: a 401 interceptor with single-flight dedup (N concurrent 401s trigger one refresh) and an explicit onSessionExpired failure path, rather than relying on Amplify's silent auto-refresh.

cost_evidence.basis: Refresh is a single bare fetchAuthSession() call site to own, but with no boundary present, adding single-flight and a failure path means introducing the seam, not filling an existing onRefresh slot.

cognito.note: cognito:groups / cognito:username and fetchUserAttributes / custom: attributes read across UserBadge, AdminPanel, and Profile — no adapter localizing them.

identity_provider.recommended_seam: Localize Cognito-specific surface (groups, custom attributes, fetchUserAttributes) inside a single adapter; the rest of the app speaks a domain Principal and OIDC/OAuth2 vocabulary, not cognito:* claims.

cost_evidence.basis: Cognito-specific surface (cognito:groups, cognito:username, custom: attributes, fetchUserAttributes) is read inline across three app-layer files with nothing localizing it; a provider swap touches every one of these call sites.

cognito.note: Authorization decisions read idToken.payload['cognito:groups'] inline with hard-coded role strings; the ID token authorizes the API.

authorization.recommended_seam: Map claims to a domain Principal at the boundary and route authorization through a policy layer instead of inline cognito:groups reads; attach the access token (not the ID token) as the API Authorization header so identity and authorization decouple.

cost_evidence.basis: Authorization reads idToken.payload['cognito:groups'] inline with hard-coded role strings in two components, and the ID token authorizes the API; a move to a policy layer plus access tokens has no single place to change.

judgment_calls.question: Is a token-storage change actually on the table — e.g. a move to HttpOnly cookies, an encrypted store, or session cookies?
judgment_calls.context: Storage is the default localStorage today. Whether that should change is roadmap, not code; and a change here is what breaks Amplify's silent refresh (see refresh).

judgment_calls.question: Is owning refresh (401-interceptor + single-flight + explicit onSessionExpired) on the roadmap?
judgment_calls.context: Refresh is inherited vendor magic today. Refresh changes are usually downstream of a storage move — likelihood is a human call.

judgment_calls.question: Is a provider swap away from Cognito realistically on the table in the foreseeable roadmap, and how much Cognito-specific behavior are you willing to keep?
judgment_calls.context: Cognito-specific surface is scattered across app code; the cost of a swap turns on how much of it you intend to preserve versus localize. Both are roadmap and appetite calls.

judgment_calls.question: Are authorization-model changes planned (RBAC/ABAC or finer permissions), or a move from the ID token to the access token for API authorization?
judgment_calls.context: Authorization is inline claim reads with the ID token authorizing the API. What backend contracts depend on the current ID-token choice is not visible in this code.

judgment_calls.question: What is the true retrofit cost in this codebase — the real call-site count once the app grows, current test coverage, and team bandwidth?
judgment_calls.context: The audit supplies mechanical cost evidence (boundary quality, spread of coupling, confirmed call sites); the time-to-complete depends on facts only the maintainer holds.

synthesis.posture: heavily calcified — no boundary; vendor shape leaks across all four axes

headline.text: The one file that looks like a seam — lib/auth-helpers.ts — hands back Amplify's AuthSession unchanged, so the vendor's shape reaches every caller; combined with the ID token (not the access token) going out as the API Authorization header, both an auth-model change and a provider swap are cross-cutting rewrites today, not local edits.
